newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property market won't dive-Cheung Kong.
newsitem.headline: HK property market won't dive-Cheung Kong.

text.p: Property developer Cheung Kong (Holdings) said on Thursday it did not expect Hong Kong's property market to plunge following the government's recently announced measures aimed at cooling down the sector.
"I don't believe it is possible for the property market to fall much," chairman Li Ka-shing told reporters. "There is still big demand in the property market."
For instance, about 90 percent of buyers of Cheung Kong's recently launched Kingswood Villas flats in the New Territories were end users, he said.
Last month, the government extended the presale period for unfinished flats to 15 months before completion from 12 months.
Developers will also have to put uncompleted flats on to the market within six months of the government granting approval for presales, and to release at least 20 percent in each batch.
Li said his company would cooperate with the government if the measures did not interfere with the free economic system.
